title: Sarge, in the barracks
description: A shaggy black gibbon, backlit so its face is in shadow, stands on all fours on a pale curved surface with a pink cloth behind it, long arms hunched — a comic little gorilla. "This is Sarge. I think this is in the barracks in my bed with the mosquito net around, maybe." And: "Location: Ton Suhn Nhut."
researchNotes: Two comments of 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0152-c18308362.json, -c18308364.json), and they close a question the guide had kept open in the wrong shape. The interview list had two animals — 'the monkey' Sarge of VN-0017, whom Ron hated, and 'the black gibbon' of this frame, unnamed — and asked whose the gibbon was. Larry's answer is that this is Sarge: one animal, a gibbon, called a monkey in the way anyone would. The survey's 'fibreglass cowling or hull' under the animal becomes, in his reading, the bedding of his own bunk under its mosquito net (VN-0084 shows the bunk). The probe is retired.
